subject.title: Memory MVP: define SQLite schema and canonical record model

question: Should memory-core move durable memory from Markdown-as-canonical storage to a plugin-owned typed SQLite record model for the MVP, and what migration, provenance, review, forget, and CLI contracts must be part of that first version?
rationale: This defines persistent user and agent memory state and controls several open Memory MVP follow-ups, so automation should not choose the durable schema or migration boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP contract
options.body: Define the v1 record/status/revision/provenance model first, then implement schema and migration boundaries in memory-core.

options.title: Keep Markdown canonical for now
options.body: Continue using SQLite for search/index/cache state and narrow this issue to docs or retrieval-specific follow-up work.

options.title: Defer until memory convergence
options.body: Leave this as design backlog until maintainers choose the recommended memory plugin path described in VISION.md.

recommendation.title: Approve plugin-owned SQLite MVP contract
recommendation.body: Define the v1 record/status/revision/provenance model first, then implement schema and migration boundaries in memory-core.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent current-main history on memory schema, memory-core internals, and memory docs touched by this decision.
